newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian govt to target new mineral areas.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian govt to target new mineral areas.

text.p: The Australian government will spend A$1.2 billion on studies of three new prospective mineral exploration areas aimed at lifting the export potential of the nation's resources and energy industries, Federal Resources Minister Warwick Parer said on Thursday.

"After talking with the states, the Commonwealth has now decided to pursue three new province studies - in central western New South Wales, western Tasmania and the Gawler Craton area in South Australia," Parer said in a speech.
Parer was outlining his government's plans to a Committee for the Economic Development of Australia (CEDA) seminar.
"The Commonwealth has committed A$1.2 billion over the next four years for studies of (these) prospective regions," he said.
"We expect the state governments and industry will make equivalent contributions," he said.

Parer also said a study of the northern goldfields province of Western Australia was currently being completed and could lift mineral revenue from gold and nickel in that area to A$4 billion a year from the present A$1.8 billion.
Parer said exploration spending in the northern goldfields province should increase markedly from the present A$100 million a year with new project investment exceeding A$900 million.
"Government and industry are evaluating funding options for upgrading road and rail infrastructure," he said.
"There will be more studies into power, water, telecommunications, town services, airport development and skilled labour," he said.
Parer said development of Queensland's Carpentaria-Mt Isa mineral province meant the area was now in a position to evolve into a regional centre for heavy engineering and construction.

Following construction of a A$400 million gas pipeline from the Pilbara region of Western Australia to the northern goldfields area, economics of downstream mineral processing would be enhanced, he said.
Parer also said the Australian government would not accept fixed targets being imposed unilaterally from overseas for greenhouse gas emissions.
"What we will not accept is fixed targets imposed on us by European nations and, I may say, aided and abetted by the United States," Parer said.
He said the Australian government was also determined to encourage the minerals industry's push to add even more value to its products in Australia.
Parer said his department had set up a new unit to take a co-ordinating role in promoting value-adding and assist industry by combining commodities, technology and engineering expertise.
